subject: He saw the fire. Then he went back to bed.
proposed_preheader_not_jetpack_native: A diary from 1666 shows why seeing, hearing and recording are three different things.
proposed_custom_excerpt_not_installed: A fire, a mistaken first impression, and a 1666 witness's diary. What a seven-day focus log can learn from historical evidence.

sources.label: Pepys diary selections, 2 and 4 September 1666 — The National Archives
Evelyn diary selections — The National Archives
Original shorthand diary artefact — Pepys Library / Great Fire collection
Stone et al., BMJ (2002), patient paper-diary timing
NIH NCCIH, Meditation and Mindfulness: Effectiveness and Safety

evidence.claim: Pepys described waking around 3 a.m., looking at a fire and returning to bed on September 2, 1666
evidence.scope: historical firsthand diary extract; no claim exact writing hour

evidence.claim: Pepys distinguished material reported by Jane, the Lieutenant and sights observed on the riverside
evidence.scope: attributed to narrator; reported house loss and origin not independently verified

evidence.claim: John Evelyn recorded the fire from another location
evidence.scope: second eyewitness perspective; no exact temporal synchronization claim

evidence.claim: Pepys Library holds an original 1666 entry in shorthand
evidence.scope: artefact record; reproduction image not used because permission required

evidence.claim: Stone et al BMJ 2002 reported 90% vs 11% paper diary compliance in a 30-minute window; 20% for wider window
evidence.scope: forty paper subjects; 40 electronic; not a meditation trial or population memory falsehood rate

evidence.claim: NCCIH describes a varied body of mindfulness/meditation evidence and potential negative effects
evidence.scope: does not establish any specific commercial recording or seven-day personal result
